sci: Mytilidae and several other bivalve families
ov: Bivalve molluscs of salt and fresh water with long, uneven shells, often dark blue, black or brown. Marine mussels cling in clumps to wave-washed rocks with strong byssal threads, the “beard”. They filter plankton from the water, and many are farmed for food.

why.et: Eaten by people, and blue mussels are farmed intensively.

rg: Temperate and tropical coasts worldwide, plus lakes, rivers and ponds; a few live at deep-sea hydrothermal vents.
df: Plankton and other tiny particles filtered from the water.
fx: Freshwater mussel larvae hitch a ride on fish, living on their gills or fins for two to five weeks.
Mussels can tie down a predatory dog whelk with their threads until it starves.
